magpylib-studio.pythonPath.description: Python interpreter used to run the magpylib-studio engine. Empty = auto-detect (.venv next to the workspace, then python3).

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_listObjects
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the objects in the current Magpylib Studio scene, depth-first. Returns an array of {id, type, label, parent}; 'parent' is the id of the containing Collection (type 'Collection' groups other objects) or null at scene root. The Studio engine starts automatically - never ask the user whether it is running or what the object ids are; call this tool to find out (an empty array just means the scene is empty).

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_getSchema
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get the JSON Schema describing every editable style property of one magpylib scene object (valid dotted paths, types, allowed values). Use it to find the correct path/value before calling the apply edit tool.

object_id.description: Id of the scene object, as returned by the list objects tool.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_addObject
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Add ONE new object to the Magpylib Studio scene; to create several objects use the batch tool in a single call instead. 'type' is a dotted magpylib class path like 'magnet.Cuboid', 'magnet.Cylinder', 'magnet.Sphere', 'current.Circle' or 'Sensor'. 'params' are the constructor kwargs (e.g. polarization, dimension/diameter, position; a Sensor position may be a list of [x,y,z] points forming a path). 'rotations' optionally rotates the object after construction (e.g. Halbach arrangements: orbit with anchor 0, then spin in place). Type 'Collection' creates a group; pass 'parent' (a Collection id) to nest an object inside a group - rotations on a Collection rotate the whole group. On failure the result contains the constructor/validation error - fix and retry. Note: on magnets the default magnetization coloring masks the base 'color' style - for a visible solid color also include 'magnetization.mode': 'arrow'. VALUES MAY BE EXPRESSIONS: any number here can instead be a string starting with '=' naming the scene's variables, e.g. "=gap" or [0, 0, "=gap*2"] - use one whenever the user describes a quantity as a parameter or repeats it across objects, so changing it later moves everything at once. The variable must already exist (set variable tool). Strings without '=' stay literal, so an axis is still 'z'. For a ring, a circular array or a Halbach arrangement, do NOT add the magnets one by one: add ONE magnet inside a Collection and call the duplicate around tool, which keeps the count editable.

object_id.description: New unique id for the object (used as the variable name in generated scripts).

style.description: Optional style, dotted paths to values, e.g. {"label": "Ball", "color": "green"}.

parent.description: Optional id of a Collection to nest this object inside; omit for scene root.

rotations.description: Optional rotations applied in order after construction. Each: {"angle": degrees, "axis": "x"|"y"|"z", "anchor": 0 or [x,y,z]}; omit 'anchor' to spin in place, anchor 0 orbits the origin.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_removeObject
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Remove one object from the Magpylib Studio scene by id. To empty the whole scene use the clear scene tool; to remove several (but not all) objects use the batch tool - never chain single removals.

object_id.description: Id of the scene object to remove, as returned by the list objects tool.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_setParam
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Set a constructor parameter of a magpylib scene object - position, dimension, diameter, polarization, ... Use this to move or resize objects (style edits use the apply edit tool instead). On failure the result contains the error - fix and retry. VALUES MAY BE EXPRESSIONS: any number here can instead be a string starting with '=' naming the scene's variables, e.g. "=gap" or [0, 0, "=gap*2"] - use one whenever the user describes a quantity as a parameter or repeats it across objects, so changing it later moves everything at once. The variable must already exist (set variable tool). Strings without '=' stay literal, so an axis is still 'z'.

object_id.description: Id of the scene object, as returned by the list objects tool.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_getField
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Compute the total magnetic field of all sources in the Magpylib Studio scene, in SI units (B in tesla, H in A/m, coordinates in meters). With no input it evaluates along the scene's sensor path; pass 'points' [[x,y,z], ...] to evaluate at specific locations instead - a list of points on a plane gives you a field map to reason about. Returns {field, unit, points, values ([Bx,By,Bz] per point), magnitude}. Use this for quantitative questions ('what is B at the center?', 'how uniform is the bore?') and to MEASURE the effect of scene edits - after editing, call it again and compare.

sensor_id.description: Optional Sensor id to evaluate along; defaults to the first sensor in the scene.

points.description: Optional explicit observer points in meters, e.g. [[0,0,0],[0,0,0.5]]; overrides sensor_id.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_undo
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Undo the most recent scene change(s) - style edits, adds, removes, moves, loads; a whole batch is one step. Use when the user asks to undo/revert, or to roll back your own edit that had an unwanted effect. Returns {ok, error?}.

steps.description: How many history steps to undo (default 1).

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_rotate
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Rotate a scene object by 'angle' degrees about 'axis'. Pass anchor 0 (or [x,y,z]) to ORBIT that point instead of spinning in place - Halbach-style arrangements orbit and spin by the same angle. A list of angles creates an animation path (use start: -1 to append to the existing path). Works on Collections too, rotating the whole group. Prefer the batch tool for many objects. VALUES MAY BE EXPRESSIONS: any number here can instead be a string starting with '=' naming the scene's variables, e.g. "=gap" or [0, 0, "=gap*2"] - use one whenever the user describes a quantity as a parameter or repeats it across objects, so changing it later moves everything at once. The variable must already exist (set variable tool). Strings without '=' stay literal, so an axis is still 'z'.

angle.description: Degrees; a list of degrees creates a path.

anchor.description: Orbit this point: 0 for the origin, or [x,y,z]. Omit to spin in place.

start.description: Path index to apply from; -1 appends to the current path.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_move
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Move a scene object by a RELATIVE displacement [dx,dy,dz] in meters. A list of displacements creates an animation path (use start: -1 to append). To set an absolute position instead, use the set position tool. Works on Collections, moving the whole group. VALUES MAY BE EXPRESSIONS: any number here can instead be a string starting with '=' naming the scene's variables, e.g. "=gap" or [0, 0, "=gap*2"] - use one whenever the user describes a quantity as a parameter or repeats it across objects, so changing it later moves everything at once. The variable must already exist (set variable tool). Strings without '=' stay literal, so an axis is still 'z'.

start.description: Path index to apply from; -1 appends to the current path.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_setTransform
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Set an object's ABSOLUTE position and/or orientation in world coordinates (meters, degrees). 'position' is [x,y,z] or a path [[x,y,z],...]; 'orientation' is a rotation vector [rx,ry,rz] in degrees. Use the move/rotate tools for relative changes. VALUES MAY BE EXPRESSIONS: any number here can instead be a string starting with '=' naming the scene's variables, e.g. "=gap" or [0, 0, "=gap*2"] - use one whenever the user describes a quantity as a parameter or repeats it across objects, so changing it later moves everything at once. The variable must already exist (set variable tool). Strings without '=' stay literal, so an axis is still 'z'.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_clearScene
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Remove ALL objects from the Magpylib Studio scene in one call. Always use this instead of removing objects one by one when the user wants to clear/clean/empty the scene.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_batch
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Apply several Magpylib Studio scene operations in ONE call - always prefer this over chaining single tool calls when creating, editing, or removing multiple objects (e.g. building an array of magnets). Operations run in order; failures don't stop the rest. The result lists per-operation outcomes ({ok, error?}) - fix failed ones and retry only those. Batchable methods: add_object, remove_object, move_object (reparent into/out of Collections: {object_id, parent?}), apply_edit, set_param, move, rotate, set_transform, clear_path, reset_style, clear_scene (their params match the corresponding single tools). Batchable methods now also include set_variable, remove_variable and duplicate_around, so a whole parametric scene - variables, the objects written in terms of them, then the arrangements - can be built in one undoable call.

params.description: Arguments for the method, same shape as the corresponding single tool (e.g. {"object_id": "m1", "type": "magnet.Cuboid", "params": {...}} for add_object).

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_applyEdit
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Set one style property on a magpylib scene object using a dotted path (e.g. 'color', 'magnetization.arrow.width'); for several style edits at once prefer the batch tool. The value is validated by magpylib; on failure the result contains the validation error - correct the path/value and retry. The Studio view refreshes automatically. Path visualization styles (the line/markers drawn along an object's movement path, e.g. a sensor sweep) live under 'path.*': 'path.line.color', 'path.marker.color', 'path.show'. Note: on magnets, magnetization coloring (a blue-white-red gradient) is shown by default and masks the base 'color' - when the user wants a visible solid color, also set 'magnetization.mode' to 'arrow' (or 'magnetization.show' to false).

object_id.description: Id of the scene object, as returned by the list objects tool.

value.description: New value for the property (string, number, boolean, or array as required by the schema).

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_getVariables
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the scene's variables with what each was written as and what it currently resolves to. Call this before writing an expression, to see which names exist. Any numeric value in this scene may be an EXPRESSION over the document's variables instead of a number: a string starting with '=', e.g. "=gap", "=360/n", [0, 0, "=gap*2"]. Anything without the '=' is a literal, so an axis stays 'z'. Expressions may use + - * / ** and sqrt/sin/cos/atan2/radians/degrees/min/max/abs/round plus pi/e/tau. Every variable used must already exist (create it with the set variable tool first) or the call fails with "unknown variable".

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_setVariable
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Define or change one named value the scene can be written in terms of, so that editing it moves everything that refers to it. Use this for any quantity the user describes as a parameter, or that repeats across objects (a gap, a radius, a magnet count, a step angle). Values are unitless SI, as magpylib uses: metres, tesla, amperes, degrees. 'value' is a number, or an expression over the OTHER variables ("=gap*2"); a variable cannot refer to itself. Changing a variable rebuilds every object written in terms of it. Any numeric value in this scene may be an EXPRESSION over the document's variables instead of a number: a string starting with '=', e.g. "=gap", "=360/n", [0, 0, "=gap*2"]. Anything without the '=' is a literal, so an axis stays 'z'. Expressions may use + - * / ** and sqrt/sin/cos/atan2/radians/degrees/min/max/abs/round plus pi/e/tau. Every variable used must already exist (create it with the set variable tool first) or the call fails with "unknown variable".

name.description: Variable name: letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit, and not a built-in like 'pi' or 'sqrt'.

value.description: A number, or an expression over the other variables such as "=gap*2".

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_duplicateAround
languageModelTools.displayName: Duplicate a magpylib object around an axis
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Arrange ONE object into a ring of evenly spaced copies about an axis, recorded as a single event rather than as N separate objects - so the count stays one number to change. STRONGLY PREFER this over adding magnets one by one in a loop whenever the user asks for a ring, a circular array, or a Halbach arrangement. 'count' includes the original and may be a variable ("=n"). 'spin' is extra rotation in place per copy index: 0 leaves every copy facing the same way, and a Halbach ring is spin = 360/count (pass "=360/n" to keep it tied to the count). The object MUST already be inside a Collection - create one and pass it as 'parent' when adding the object - because that is where the copies go. The copies are generated, not listed as editable objects: change the original, the count or the variables instead. Any numeric value in this scene may be an EXPRESSION over the document's variables instead of a number: a string starting with '=', e.g. "=gap", "=360/n", [0, 0, "=gap*2"]. Anything without the '=' is a literal, so an axis stays 'z'. Expressions may use + - * / ** and sqrt/sin/cos/atan2/radians/degrees/min/max/abs/round plus pi/e/tau. Every variable used must already exist (create it with the set variable tool first) or the call fails with "unknown variable".

object_id.description: Id of the object to arrange. Must be inside a Collection.

count.description: Total number of copies including the original, or an expression such as "=n".

axis.description: Axis to arrange about: 'x', 'y', 'z', or a vector [x,y,z]. Default 'z'.

anchor.description: Point the copies orbit: 0 for the origin, or [x,y,z]. Default 0.

spin.description: Extra in-place rotation per copy index, in degrees. 0 for a plain ring, "=360/n" for a Halbach ring.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_sweep
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Rebuild the scene once per value of a variable and read the field at each, for answering questions like 'how does B at the sensor vary with the gap'. Returns one step per value with the field vectors and their magnitudes (SI: tesla for B, A/m for H). The scene is left on the value it started from and no undo step is recorded. Requires a variable the scene is actually written in terms of - define one with the set variable tool and use it in the objects first, otherwise every step is identical. Observers: 'sensor_id' names a Sensor, 'points' gives explicit [[x,y,z]] positions; without either it uses the first sensor in the scene.

variable.description: Name of the variable to vary.

sensor_id.description: Id of a Sensor to read at. Optional.

points.description: Explicit observation points [[x,y,z], ...] in metres. Optional.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_setVariableBounds
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Limit a variable. Hard bounds ('min'/'max') are enforced: any value outside them is refused, including one the variable reaches through an expression - use them for what is physically or geometrically impossible, such as a negative gap or fewer than one magnet. Soft bounds ('soft_min'/'soft_max') only say which range is worth exploring; values outside stay legal, and this is what a slider or a sweep should span. Soft bounds must lie inside hard ones. Call with no bounds to clear them. Values are unitless SI.

soft_min.description: Low end of the interesting range. Optional.

soft_max.description: High end of the interesting range. Optional.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_getEvents
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the scene's construction history in order: each event's id, index, what it did, and - for any the last rebuild could not apply - an 'error' saying why. Call this before editing history, to see what is there and what is already broken. The scene's construction history: doc['events'] is the whole scene, not a side record - `create` events bring objects into being, `remove`/`reparent` and the transforms say what happened to them afterwards, and the object tree is derived from folding all of it. Rebuilding always folds the whole log, so changing an early event re-applies everything after it.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_editEvent
languageModelTools.displayName: Edit a past magpylib scene event
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Change one past event and re-apply everything recorded after it - the way to answer 'make that rotation 30 degrees instead' without redoing the work that followed. 'changes' holds only the fields to replace, e.g. {"angle": 30} or {"count": "=n"}; values may be expressions over the variables. Editing what an object *is* (its params or style) is NOT done here - use the set param or apply edit tools, which edit its create event in place. If the edit leaves later events with nothing to act on, it still applies and returns them under 'broken'; if the edited event itself cannot replay, it is rolled back and reported. The scene's construction history: doc['events'] is the whole scene, not a side record - `create` events bring objects into being, `remove`/`reparent` and the transforms say what happened to them afterwards, and the object tree is derived from folding all of it. Rebuilding always folds the whole log, so changing an early event re-applies everything after it.

event_id.description: Id of the event, from the list history tool (e.g. 'e12').

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_removeEvent
languageModelTools.displayName: Remove a past magpylib scene event
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Drop one event from the history and rebuild without it - use it to undo something that happened early without losing what came after. Whatever depended on it comes back under 'broken' rather than blocking the removal. To delete an OBJECT use the remove object tool instead; that records a removal rather than erasing how the object came to be. The scene's construction history: doc['events'] is the whole scene, not a side record - `create` events bring objects into being, `remove`/`reparent` and the transforms say what happened to them afterwards, and the object tree is derived from folding all of it. Rebuilding always folds the whole log, so changing an early event re-applies everything after it.

event_id.description: Id of the event to drop.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_moveEvent
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Move one event to another position in the history. This is a real change, not a cosmetic one: transforms do not commute, so an orbit followed by a move lands somewhere else than a move followed by an orbit. An event cannot be placed above the create event of the object it acts on - it would have nothing to act on, and comes back under 'broken'. The scene's construction history: doc['events'] is the whole scene, not a side record - `create` events bring objects into being, `remove`/`reparent` and the transforms say what happened to them afterwards, and the object tree is derived from folding all of it. Rebuilding always folds the whole log, so changing an early event re-applies everything after it.

event_id.description: Id of the event to move.

index.description: Position to move it to, as listed by the list history tool.

languageModelTools.name: magpylib-studio_duplicateAlong
languageModelTools.displayName: Repeat a magpylib object in a row
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Arrange ONE object into a line of evenly spaced copies, recorded as a single event rather than as N separate objects - the linear pattern to the duplicate around tool's circular one. STRONGLY PREFER this over adding objects one by one whenever the user asks for a row, a line, an array or a grid of something. 'count' includes the original and may be a variable ("=n"); 'step' is the displacement between neighbours in metres, e.g. [0.005, 0, 0], and its components may be expressions. FOR A GRID: pattern the object along one direction, then pattern the Collection holding it along the other - two linear patterns compose into a rectangular one, and both counts stay editable. The object must already be inside a Collection, which is where the copies go. The copies are generated, not listed as editable objects: change the original, the count or the variables instead.

object_id.description: Id of the object to repeat. Must be inside a Collection.

count.description: Total copies including the original, or an expression such as "=n".

step.description: Displacement between neighbouring copies as [dx, dy, dz] in metres; components may be expressions.
